title: Cokernels of maps between finite-presentation modules are finite presentation
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, let $\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $f:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ be $\mathcal O_X$-linear. If $\mathcal G$ is of finite type (locally a quotient of $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus m}$ with $m$ finite) and $\mathcal H$ is of finite presentation (locally the cokernel of $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}$ with $r,n$ finite) [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], then the cokernel of $f$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ is of finite presentation. In particular this holds when both $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal H$ are of finite presentation.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 0H96 (lemma-cokernel-finite-finite-presentation), lines 1431-1450; used in Properties, Lemma 01PJ, lines 3112-3116

proof.text: Choose the finite local presentation data q of H. On each open q.X i, the finite generators of its presentation, followed by the restricted cokernel map of f, give an epimorphism to the restriction of cokernel f. The intermediate kernel-composite theorem gives finite type of its kernel. Choose finite local generators of that kernel, restrict the original finite generators, and use preservation of cokernels and free modules to construct finite presentations on the refined cover. This construction is proved in the private helper isFinitePresentation_of_generators_kernel. Locality of finite presentation glues the presentations to prove the main theorem. Apply finite presentation implies finite type to G for the special case.
